% footnotes — two footnotes, each marked in the body and set at the foot of the page.
%
% A footnote is two pieces of text far apart on the page: a raised mark inside a
% sentence, and a note in smaller type below a rule. GFM writes them as a reference
% and a definition, which is what the gold file holds. A reader that keeps the note
% where it is drawn puts it after the last paragraph as if it were body text, and one
% that keeps the mark as a digit glues it to the word before.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{lmodern}
\usepackage[paperwidth=6in,paperheight=4in,margin=0.6in]{geometry}
\pagestyle{empty}
\begin{document}
The survey counted forty species on the island\footnote{Counted over three summers,
from 2019 to 2021.} and found nesting sites for twelve of them.

Most of the nests were on the western cliffs, where the ground is hardest to
reach.\footnote{The eastern shore is open to grazing.}
\end{document}
